name: Shareholder yield
summary: Companies paying out 12%+ of their market cap a year through dividends and buybacks, with positive free cash flow.
how_to_read: Two filters must both pass: shareholder yield (dividend yield plus net buyback yield, trailing twelve months) of at least 12%, and a positive free-cash-flow yield. Glint's version leaves out debt paydown, which Faber includes, so a company paying down debt instead of buying back shares scores lower here than in the book. The FCF test asks whether payouts are covered by cash the business made.
misses: Payouts funded by new debt: the screen doesn't check, so look at net debt too.
Buybacks that just offset stock pay: net buybacks subtract only cash raised from issuing shares, not shares handed out as stock-based pay, so they still count in full. Check the share-count change.
Why the yield is high: it can mean a falling share price as easily as a generous company.
source: Faber, Shareholder Yield: A Better Approach to Dividend Investing (2013). Glint's version excludes debt paydown
